newsitem.title: ITALY: SOCCER-JUVENTUS LEAVE PARMA LITTLE HOPE OF TITLE.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-JUVENTUS LEAVE PARMA LITTLE HOPE OF TITLE.

text.p: An imperious Juventus, helped by outgoing champions and old rivals AC Milan, dealt Parma's serie A title hopes a hammer blow on Thursday.
The European Cup holders, holding their fire until the second half in Turin, thrashed lowly Piacenza 4-1 with French midfield magician Zinedine Zidane leading the way.

Second-placed Parma, who play Juventus in a potentially season-deciding match at the Delle Alpi stadium on Sunday, surrendered an early lead to a late Milan penalty and drew 1-1 in a battle between teacher and former pupil.
Milan coach Arrigo Sacchi was young Parma coach Carlo Ancelotti's former mentor at Milan.
The draw left Parma six points adrift with three games remaining so if Juventus win on Sunday they will clinch their 24th league title in their centenary year.

Parma's best bet looks to be a place in the European Cup next season as runners-up. But even that became less certain after Inter beat relegated Reggiana 3-1 in Milan and narrowed the gap between second and third place to two points.
England midfielder Paul Ince, who has yet to announce whether he will be staying at Inter next season, scored twice.
But Inter, who play a UEFA Cup final second leg in Milan next week, were less than impressive and took 43 minutes to score. France's Youri Djorkaeff missed a 34th minute penalty.
The 36 goals scored was the highest tally in serie A in one day this season but way behind the record of 48.
The night was a huge blow to Parma, who have never won the title but looked on course to cut the gap at the top to two points when Enrico Chiesa scored in the sixth minute direct from a free kick.
They led 1-0 at the break, having missed other opportunities, while lacklustre Juventus were struggling 0-0 with a defiant Piacenza.
But if ever proof were needed that soccer is a game of two halves, Juventus were a team reborn after the break.
Coach Marcello Lippi took off surprise starter Alessandro Del Piero and replaced him with Zidane.
"There's no point making tactical considerations," Lippi said later. "The maths is what counts and we know that we can only win the title by winning."
Within six minutes the Frenchman, served handsomely by compatriot Didier Deschamps, had the ball in the net.
Two minutes later Christian Vieri made it 2-0 from a cross by Angelo Di Livio.
Pasquale Luiso gave Piacenza, now in deep trouble on the edge of the relegation zone, hope in the 55th minute before the Juventus wave rolled over the visitors yet again.
Vladimir Jugovic made it 3-1 after 78 minutes with a rocketing free kick and Vieri bagged his second in the 87th.
Meanwhile, Milan's Demetrio Albertini calmly levelled the score for his troubled team at Parma with a 70th minute penalty after Stefano Eranio was felled in the area.
In the relegation zone there was hope for Cagliari, who thrashed Fiorentina 4-1, and Perugia. They beat 10-man Bologna 5-1 after Carlo Nervo went off in the 34th minute.
Roma finally gave 74-year stopgap coach Nils Liedholm his first win at the helm, a 4-0 thrashing of Atalanta while city rivals Lazio beat Napoli 3-2 at the Olympic Stadium.

Udinese, reduced to 10 men five minutes from the end, remained on course for their best finish since the early 1980s, moving up to fifth and into the UEFA Cup places after a 3-0 demolition of second from bottom Verona.
